name: Newegg Refreshed (first-party refurbished) Intel Arc B580 12GB tier
price_basis: REFURBISHED via Newegg's own 'Newegg Refreshed' tier, bare PCIe consumer card. $199.99 = ONIX ODYSSEY B580 12GB, and also the Intel Arc B580 Limited Edition. Other refreshed asks: ASRock Challenger B580 $259.99, Acer Nitro B580 $249.99. Captured 2026-10-03. For comparison the same page shows NEW ASRock Challenger B580 at $329.99 (list $355.15) and NEW Intel B580 Limited Edition at $590.00. Warranty: Newegg Refreshed carries its own programme warranty, distinct from and shorter than a full manufacturer warranty - the exact term was not published in the extracted page.
notes: The only first-party refurb channel in this slice that publishes live prices for consumer accelerators, and the contrast with eBay used is the point: refreshed $199.99-$259.99 versus used $290.00-$499.00 versus new $329.99-$590.00. Buying USED Intel silicon is strictly dominated - the refurbished tier is 27% to 34% below new and 31% to 55% below used. That ordering (refurb < used < new) is the opposite of what most people assume, and it holds because used consumer cards here are thin supply with no warranty while the refurb tier is a steady pipeline. AVAILABILITY CAVEAT, important: every refreshed unit in the captured listing was marked OUT OF STOCK. Newegg Refreshed on B580 is a browse-able but rarely actually purchasable tier - treat these as achievable prices, not as items in stock today. This also means availability is recorded as unknown rather than in-stock despite prices showing.
